name: Generate unit tests for GitHub pull requests with Claude and run them in CI

parameters.content:
## Generate unit tests for GitHub pull requests with Claude and run them in CI

Engineering teams with thin test coverage who want tests proposed automatically on every change.

### How it works
Trigger: PR events on the main repositories; a label can request generation on demand.
1. Receive the PR and diff
2. Find untested changed functions
3. Assemble context
4. Generate tests
5. Run in CI
6. Keep what passes and adds coverage
7. Open the companion PR
8. Learn from reviews
Every AI step is followed by a "Needs a person?" gate that parks low-confidence items.

### Setup
1. Open "Config (edit me)" and fill in the fields (names, approver, quiet hours, thresholds).
2. Add credentials: Anthropic, plus GitHub Actions / GitLab CI, Jest / pytest / Go test / JUnit.
3. Run once with test_mode on, read the output, then switch the trigger on.

### Customization tips
Set the test framework and directories in the Config node; swap the GitHub nodes for GitLab if that is where the code lives.
Guardrail to keep: Generated tests are proposed in a separate PR; nothing merges without an engineer's review.

Full blueprint: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/unit-test-generation/

## 1. Receive the PR and diff
Changed files and hunks; PRs from bots or with a skip label are ignored

nodes.name: Section: 1. Receive the PR and diff

parameters.content:
## 2. Find untested changed functions
Coverage report from CI mapped to the diff: functions and branches that changed and have no covering test

## 3. Assemble context
The changed file, its imports, existing test files for the module (for conventions and fixtures), and the test framework config

## 4. Generate tests
Tests per function in the repo's framework and style, covering the happy path, edge cases visible in the code, and error paths; structured output with one test file per source file

## 5. Run in CI
Generated tests pushed to a branch and run with the existing suite; results and the coverage delta collected

## 6. Keep what passes and adds coverage
Tests that fail are discarded (or retried once with the failure output); tests that pass but add no coverage are dropped; flaky tests (pass/fail on rerun) are dropped

nodes.name: Section: 6. Keep what passes and adds coverage

parameters.content:
## 7. Open the companion PR
A PR against the original branch with the surviving tests, a summary of what they cover and the coverage delta, assigned to the original author

## 8. Learn from reviews
Weekly: acceptance rate of generated tests, common edits reviewers make, and coverage trend on changed code; prompts adjusted from the edits

## Fill this in first
Every later node reads these values. Keep test_mode on for the first week.

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Generate tests" step of the AI Unit Test Generation workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: Tests per function in the repo's framework and style, covering the happy path, edge cases visible in the code, and error paths; structured output with one test file per source file.

Rules:
- Generated tests are proposed in a separate PR; nothing merges without an engineer's review.
- Only tests that pass, are not flaky, and add coverage are proposed — the run is the filter.
- The agent cannot modify source code, only add test files.
- Repositories can be excluded, and a self-hosted model is available for sensitive code.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.
